newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves new houses for settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves new houses for settlement.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai has approved a plan, frozen by the previous Labour government, to build 1,800 more homes in a Jewish settlement in the West Bank, a settlement leader said.

"It received all the permits from the previous government and I am glad the defence minister finally approved it," Pinhas Wallerstein, head of the council of Jewish settlers in the West Bank and Gaza, said in remarks on Army Radio on Wednesday.
He said the 1,800 housing units would be built in Matityahu, a settlement for ultra-Orthodox Jews near the pre-1967 Middle East war border between Israel and the West Bank.
"I understand that once all the planning stages are completed, the investor can start building," Wallerstein said.
Army Radio said Mordechai gave his approval last week. The news broke on the day he was due to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for the first time, in self-ruled Gaza.
The Peace Now group, a strong opponent of Jewish settlement in occupied territories, said the homes would be built on land near two Palestinian villages.
"The villagers regard this land as theirs...when they see the houses going up, I suppose they will not sit quietly," Peace Now general-secretary Mossi Raz told Army Radio.

A statement from Mordechai's office carried by the radio said: "We are not talking about establishing new settlements but adding on to existing ones in the framework of infrastructure plans already approved by the previous government".

Last month, Mordechai approved several construction plans for existing settlements. His spokesman declined to say how many housing units would be built but Israeli media reports put the number at between 2,000 and 3,550.
Mordechai's moves were in line with the decision by the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel the previous administration's building freeze in the West Bank.

Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. Some 130,000 Jews have settled amidst the nearly two million Palestinians in the territories since Israel captured them in the 1967 Middle East war.
